top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation by induced proximity (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) is a new chemical mode of action: a small molecule acts as a catalytic bridge to an E3 ligase, replacing site occupancy with removal of the target. The ternary-complex mechanism and cereblon as the thalidomide target are reproduced across many laboratories, ligases and targets, and the three names span the PROTAC concept and the glue mechanism. The lack of an approved degrader is a timing risk, not a scientific defect, and the three-name cap, which excludes Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim, gives an accurate if costly citation. The genetic-code expansion prize (P003) is more mature and cleanly attributed, so it ranks second, ahead of C-N cross-coupling (P002), which sits closest to the 2010 palladium prize. Any award ranks above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Lund colleagues Linke and Somfai sit on the committee, but no direct tie to any proposed laureate is documented
